We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it
to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If you wish to
address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be heard during
the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission on a subject which
does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service, you may make your
presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission cannot, under the State of
California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item that does not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make your
statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  May 13, 2026

Call to Order
The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:01 PM on May 13, 2026, at the Alhambra Civic
Center Library, 101 South 1st Street, Alhambra, CA 91801.

I. Roll Call
Commissioners Present: Pamela Ghazale, Arabella Hernandez, Isabella Hernandez,
Katherine Quintana, Natalia Rosales
Staff Present: Brie Houghton (Deputy Director), Rosalyn Rojas (Recreation Supervisor).
Absent: Lydia Chen, Leslie Chu, Suki Li, Brendon Wu,

I. Flag Salute
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited with all members standing and participating.

III. Approval of Minutes (February 10, 2026 Meeting)
Motion to approve the February meeting minutes was made by Isabella Hernandez and seconded by Pamela
Ghazale. The motion was approved.

IV. Staff Report

Staffs Houghton and Rojas, provided an update on Camp Alhambra programming and Youth Commission
involvement opportunities.

  Key points:

    Recreation Supervisor Rojas Summer programming begins in June 1, with limited time remaining
  for independent event planning.
    Deputy Director Houghton encouraged commissioners to assist with pre-organized activities instead.
    Collaboration opportunities include:
  o Reading programs with the Alhambra Library
  o Sustainability activities (“Camp Goes Green”)
    Recreation Supervisor Rojas advises Camp Alhambra activities are primarily held on Tuesdays and
  Thursdays

  Availability Discussion:
  Due to limited availability, the following tentative volunteer dates were identified:
  June 9, 11, 16, and 18.

  Staff actions:

    Distribute detailed schedules and sign-up opportunities.
    Commissioners may select preferred volunteer dates.
    Identification materials (lanyards and name badges) will be provided.
    Photo opportunities will be coordinated with the City’s Public Information Specialist to promote the
  Youth Commission’s presence.
 V. Oral Communications
No additional public oral communications were presented.

VI. Commission Orals

    Commissioner Quintana discussed the possibility of organizing a holiday toy drive and inquired about
  additional volunteer opportunities, including food drives.
    President Ghazale expressed support for planning November and December activities in advance,
  including a potential Thanksgiving food drive and holiday card-making activities for youth.

  Staff response:

  o  Large-scale drives require significant coordination and participation. Deputy Director Houghton
  recommended partnering with schools or established community efforts at this time. The
  opportunity to organize independent drives or events may be revisited as the Youth Commission
  continues to build capacity and expand its community presence.
  o  Recreation Supervisor Rojas also discussed the return of a monthly craft activity at the Alhambra
  Farmers’ Market, which could align with holiday card-making activities and crafts with the
  youth. The Parks and Recreation Department would provide booth space and supplies.

VII. Adjournment

Recreation Supervisor Rojas calls the meeting to adjourn at 6:19 PM.
